s.g: Used to form adjectives from verbs, especially those in -ить (-itʹ).
the Alps (a mountain range in Europe)
Alaska (a state of the United States, formerly a territory)
to bottle (to seal (a liquid) into a bottle for later consumption)
to butylate (to react so as to introduce one or more butyl groups into a molecule)
a transliteration of the Georgian surname გამსახურდია (gamsaxurdia)
to nail, to fasten with nails, to board up
to earn, to knock up, to knock down, to pull down
to catch someone doing something illegal or disallowed, to catch red-handed
kapo (a prisoner in a Nazi concentration camp who was given food and privileges in return for supervising other prisoners doing forced labor)
a modern prisoner who cooperates with prison authorities in supervising fellow prisoners
Roman Catholic church (in Poland or the Baltic states)
Koschei (also Koshchei, Koshchey, Kashchei or Kashchey)
initialism of отде́льная артиллери́йская брига́да (otdélʹnaja artilleríjskaja brigáda); separate artillery brigade
to hide for a while, to take cover
to sit it out, to not participate
picture on a canvas, a decorative picture on a wall, ceiling, etc.
anachronism (person or thing which seems to belong to a different time)
to ride out, to go/get/live through; to be through, to get over (a hardship)
[with dative ‘whom?’ and accusative ‘на + by how much?’] to outlive
to dry up, to get too dry, to become parched
the English letter P/p; a pee
male or female genitalia, doodle, pussy
to start to leak, to leak
to drizzle, to fall in small drops (of rain)
administrative body of a city or township
a surname, Salye, from French, equivalent to French Saliès or Salié
synchrophasotron (type of synchrotron, a type of particle accelerator, especially one operating at the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research in Dubna from 1957 to 2003)
substantial, substantive, full of substance, rich in content, meaty
speechwriter (someone who writes speeches for others, especially as a profession)
Central Asia (a landlocked geographic area of continental central Asia comprising Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan)
cloth, broadcloth (a dense, smooth woolen or (rarely) cotton fabric)
desk, table (with a smooth cloth-covered tabletop; e.g. a card table or a billiards table)
traditional Russian women's sweater that is usually sleeveless
a female given name, Khava, from Hebrew
